write_conflict.message: your write overlaps changes made since version 1: 1 region(s) at line 5; nothing applied
write_conflict.next: Someone else changed the same lines after the version you read (or added lines at the same place), so nothing was applied; a write never merges inside a line. Run cat to read the current text (the message and details.current give its version), make your change again on that text, and write it with write --base <that version>. Or change only the lines you need with replace --lines or patch, each with --if-version <that version> (they take --if-version, not --base). details.conflicts has each region's your_lines (in your text), current_lines (in the current text), base, ours and theirs.

bad_hunk.message: hunk 0 is out of range or not on a character boundary
bad_hunk.next: An edit's ranges are out of order, out of range, off a character boundary or empty. The host computes ranges from the text it read: read again and recompute.

base_expired.message: base version 1 is unknown or no longer cached; nothing applied
base_expired.next: The version you wrote against is too old to merge from (or was never read). Never retry the same request: read the doc again (cat), redo your change on what you read, and write with that version as --base.

details.why: more changes since than the live window holds

bad_position.message: bad position: Byte(39) is not in "source"
bad_position.next: A line or position is outside the doc. Read the doc's length first (wc -l, or cat -n) and pass lines inside it.

bad_edit_frame_cap.message: bad edit: the frame is 4194400 bytes, over the 4194304-byte cap
bad_edit_frame_cap.next: The edit itself is malformed (the message says how). Fix the arguments and run it again; nothing was applied.

declined_too_large.message: live editing is off: the text doesn't fit one frame (too_large)
declined_too_large.next: The file is over the size limit for live editing (capabilities shows the limits). It opens the ordinary way: edit it with ordinary file tools, without live merging. Don't retry the live verb.

history_lost.message: nothing to undo: your undo history was lost when the doc reloaded
history_lost.next: Undo history lives in memory and was dropped when the doc unloaded or the daemon restarted. Your changes are still in the log: find one with log --by <you> and reverse it with revert <change>.
